learningObjective: Map each long-context failure mode to the technique that actually addresses it, while distinguishing positional extrapolation, dense-attention execution, and persistent serving state.
mediumRationale: A three-row semantic comparison is the smallest medium that lets readers scan from each independently growing constraint to its matching lever and explicit non-solution. Native table semantics preserve the row-wise mapping better than a routed architecture diagram.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Rejected: the lesson is a parallel three-row classification rather than a causal or temporal graph. Automatic routing would imply a pipeline and make the important one-to-one comparison harder to scan.
mediumComparison.svg: Rejected: fixed geometry adds no quantitative insight beyond the symbolic n and n-squared rates. Native text wrapping and table semantics are more robust at narrow widths.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Selected: scoped headers align each bottleneck, growth mechanism, and matching lever in accessible reading order. The existing compact comparison-table primitive supplies responsive text, theme tokens, and print behavior without runtime rendering.
mediumComparison.interaction: Rejected: toggling context length could animate cost growth, but it would hide the conceptual distinction and require assumptions about model dimensions. All three invariants fit in one static view.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected: the position-interpolation, FlashAttention, PagedAttention, and GQA papers each explain one component, but no single source figure provides the article's cross-layer comparison. Figure reuse permission was not established from the arXiv records, so no figure, prose, values, icons, or composition is copied.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected: the prose lists techniques under three headings but readers can still transfer a benefit across boundaries—for example, assuming FlashAttention reduces quadratic arithmetic or PagedAttention shrinks the logical cache. The row-wise visual makes both the matching lever and its limit explicit.

pages.insight: The preceding LLM-data slide discusses scaling laws and corpus construction, establishing that the nearby section has not yet introduced long-context execution.
The LLM-training slide names RoPE among architecture choices and BF16/FSDP for throughput, but it does not cover position extension beyond the trained range or persistent inference state.

The compute-optimization setup identifies dense attention's quadratic work and naive score-matrix memory, distinguishes I/O optimization from changing the math, and introduces the three levers of packing, FlashAttention, and sub-quadratic attention.

The sequence-packing slide removes padding waste and resets positions at document boundaries. It improves training utilization but does not extend positional generalization or reduce the per-request KV cache.

The FlashAttention slide explains exact SRAM tiling, online-softmax statistics, linear auxiliary memory, and recomputation. It directly supports the distinction between removing quadratic materialization and retaining dense quadratic arithmetic.
The neighboring sparse-attention slide changes the attention pattern to near-linear work, unlike FlashAttention's exact dense calculation, and records the task-dependent quality tradeoff.
The low-rank and kernel slide covers Linformer, Performer, and LongNet as methods that change or restrict attention math. It does not address position extrapolation or cache allocation.
The speculative-decoding slide targets serial generation latency by verifying draft tokens in parallel; it is a separate bottleneck from long-input score workspace and retained K/V state.
The mixed-precision slide reduces tensor bytes and improves throughput, supplying general memory context but not a complete long-context mechanism.

The training-and-serving summary is the closest deck analogue: it maps packing, FlashAttention, sparse or low-rank attention, speculative decoding, and mixed precision to distinct bottlenecks and names a paged KV cache. It omits RoPE extension and does not separate logical KV size from allocator fragmentation.
The re-scoring divider ends the relevant LLM optimization neighborhood and contains no long-context material.

deckReview.notes: GitHub Copilot CLI agent-4 (GPT-5.6 Sol) text-indexed all 214 physical PDF pages for long context, context window, sequence length, RoPE, position interpolation, FlashAttention, KV cache, PagedAttention, grouped-query attention, and sliding window, then read pages 96-116 as the complete language-model and optimization neighborhood. Pages 107-115 are the relevant run, with page 115 providing the closest high-level technique-to-bottleneck mapping. The deck does not combine positional extrapolation, exact attention execution, and serving-state economics in one figure. No deck artwork, wording, coordinates, or layout is reused.

sources.title: Extending Context Window of Large Language Models via Positional Interpolation
sources.usage: Used as the primary source to verify that position interpolation rescales longer position indices into the original position range and uses limited long-context fine-tuning to extend usable context.
sources.license: The public arXiv record did not establish permissive figure-reuse rights. No paper figure, equation layout, prose, benchmark value, or composition is copied; the source is cited only for the mechanism.

sources.title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
sources.usage: Used as the primary source to verify that tiled exact attention reduces HBM traffic and avoids materializing the full quadratic score and probability matrices while retaining exact dense-attention arithmetic.
sources.license: The paper's public availability and the repository's BSD-3-Clause software license were not treated as permission to reproduce paper artwork. No figure, algorithm text, benchmark, or layout is adapted.

sources.title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
sources.usage: Used as the primary systems source to verify that block-based KV-cache allocation reduces fragmentation and enables sharing while leaving the attention computation and logical per-sequence state intact.
sources.license: The arXiv record did not establish a permissive license for paper figures. The vLLM codebase is Apache-2.0, but that software license is not assumed to license paper artwork. No source figure, code, values, prose, or layout is reused.

sources.title: GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints
sources.usage: Used as the primary source to verify that grouped-query attention uses fewer key/value heads than query heads, reducing the logical KV-cache footprint and memory bandwidth relative to multi-head attention.
sources.license: No permissive figure-reuse grant was established from the public paper record. The comparison table is independently authored and reproduces no paper figure, prose, data point, or visual arrangement.

sourceReview.notes: The hardest prose-only mental model is that a headline context length intersects three independent constraints. Position methods determine whether token distances remain meaningful beyond the training range. FlashAttention determines whether exact dense attention can execute without quadratic intermediate storage, but does not remove its quadratic arithmetic. GQA and quantization reduce logical per-request KV bytes, while PagedAttention primarily reduces allocator waste and enables block reuse rather than shrinking unique K/V state. Source review also caught and corrected the article's score-matrix arithmetic: 128,000 squared FP32 values occupy about 61 GiB (65.5 GB), not 16 GB.

agentReview.summary: Read the complete article, indexed all 214 deck pages and inspected the full language-model optimization neighborhood, checked four primary papers and relevant software-license boundaries, corrected the FP32 matrix-size calculation, and selected an original semantic comparison.

implementation.accessibility: The figure uses a labelled semantic table with scoped column and row headers. Every bottleneck, growth rule, lever, and limitation is stated in text, so no meaning depends on color. The established three-column cm-grid uses compact wrapping text with no minimum width at 390 CSS pixels; shared theme variables preserve dark-mode contrast, and the existing print rules force a light high-contrast canvas and avoid page breaks inside the figure.
